_comment: Curated per-activity reference: purpose, CONFIG keys and prompt notes. The backend ActivityCatalog carries only stable OUTPUT params, not CONFIG keys; this fills that gap. It is the single source for both the MCP tools/resources and the generated activity-catalog section of the AI prompts. `description` is the one-line purpose (MCP-facing); `promptNotes` carries the extra semantics the AI prompt needs. Keys are authoritative against src/NodePilot.Engine/Activities/*.cs and Triggers/*.cs — audit against the executors when an activity config changes.

runScript.description: Run a PowerShell script (hybrid: local engine, or remote via WinRM when targetMachineId is set).
promptNotes: Step success is ERROR-based: only a terminating PowerShell error (`throw`, or `Write-Error` under the wrapper's Stop preference) fails the step. An explicit `exit N` does NOT fail it — set `successExitCodes` to make a non-zero exit a failure. The exit code is always exposed as {{step.param.exitCode}}.

Omit targetMachineId to run on the NodePilot host; set a non-local targetMachineId to run through the WinRM wrapper on that target. A local runScript may still use PowerShell remoting itself (Invoke-Command, New-PSSession).
Declare `$variableName = ...` at script scope to expose values downstream as {{thisStepId.param.variableName}}.
Write real, working PowerShell — no placeholders or pseudo-code. PowerShell 5.1/7.x compatible, non-interactive (no Read-Host/Get-Credential), avoid Write-Host.

configKeys.description: PowerShell script body. Reference upstream values as {{step.output}} — inserted already single-quoted, so do NOT wrap in quotes.
auto | runspace | pwsh | powershell. 'pwsh' spawns an external PS7 process (needed for Start-Job); 'powershell' spawns Windows PowerShell 5.1, which imported SCOrch scripts are written against.
Local-only: run process-isolated in a Windows Job Object (crash/leak containment, no orphaned processes). No-op on the remote/WinRM path.
Comma-separated exit codes treated as success (e.g. "0" or "0,1"). Makes any other non-zero exit a failure.
Isolated mode only: aggregate job memory cap.
Isolated mode only: max processes in the job.
Capture an interleaved command+output transcript as a console would show it.

promptNotes: Operates on FILES only — destructive ops assert -PathType Leaf, so a folder passed by mistake fails fast. Use folderOperation for directories.
`create` makes an empty file (truncates with -Force if it exists; refuses if a folder occupies the path).

configKeys.description: copy | move | delete | exists | create | rename.

promptNotes: Operates on FOLDERS only — destructive ops assert -PathType Container. Use fileOperation for files.
`create` makes a new directory; `list` enumerates immediate children.

configKeys.description: copy | move | delete | exists | list | create | rename.

fileHash.description: Compute or compare a file hash (remote).

configKeys.description: If set, the step compares against it and exposes {{step.param.match}}.

zipOperation.description: Create or extract a ZIP archive (remote).

configKeys.description: Source path; wildcards are allowed for compress.
status | start | stop | restart | create | delete | setStartType.
Required for setStartType: Automatic | AutomaticDelayedStart | Manual | Disabled.
get (default) | start | stop | enable | disable | register | unregister.
Trigger kind for register: once | daily | weekly | atLogon | atStartup.
Principal to run the task as (register).

promptNotes: Outputs vary by operation: single read/exists → param.value+param.type / param.exists; read without valueName or listValues → param.values+param.count; listSubKeys → param.subKeys+param.count; createKey → param.created. `deleteKey` removes the key recursively.

configKeys.description: read | write | deleteValue | deleteKey | createKey | exists | listSubKeys | listValues.
Required for write/deleteValue; optional for read/exists.
String (default) | ExpandString | Binary | DWord | MultiString | QWord. Write only.
Required for wql mode: a raw SELECT … FROM … statement.
WHERE clause for query mode; for invokeMethod it scopes to an instance method (otherwise treated as a static call).
invokeMethod arguments as a JSON object → PS hashtable; keys must be valid identifiers.
JSON array of CIM property names, e.g. ["Caption","Version"] - a comma-separated string is rejected. Projected to {{step.param.<Name>}} (+ param.count).
Absolute local path to the executable - a bare name like cmd.exe is rejected, PATH is not searched.
Block until the process exits and capture stdout/stderr/exitCode.
Comma-separated exit codes treated as success.
How long to wait for the process when waitForExit is set.
Use the shell to start the process. May be blocked by StartProgram:DisallowShellExecute.

powerManagement.description: Shut down, restart or otherwise power-control a machine (remote).

waitForCondition.description: Poll until a condition is met (hybrid; local without a target machine).
promptNotes: Each conditionType needs its own key: script → `script`, pathExists → `path`, serviceRunning → `serviceName`, portOpen → `host` + `port`, httpOk → `url`.
The `script` mode takes a PowerShell expression and does NOT support {{...}} templates. The typed modes do accept {{upstream.param.x}} — the engine quotes those values safely.

configKeys.description: PowerShell expression for conditionType=script. No {{...}} templates.

promptNotes: Do NOT use restApi to call an LLM / chat-completions endpoint — use the `llmQuery` activity instead. It handles the endpoint, key, model, token accounting and the SSRF guard for you, and never needs a hand-written API key in the node config.

configKeys.description: GET (default) | POST | PUT | PATCH | DELETE | HEAD.

promptNotes: Prefer a named `connectionRef` — raw `connectionString` and builder credentials are dev/legacy only and may be blocked by SqlActivity:RequireConnectionRef.

configKeys.description: PostgreSQL SSL mode. Defaults to VerifyFull with Trust Server Certificate=false; weaker modes are allowed only for literal loopback hosts.

promptNotes: Per-operation keys: `content` for append/prepend/insert/replaceLine (multi-line via \n); `lineNumber` (1-based) for insert/replaceLine; for `delete` exactly one of `lineRange` [from,to], `matchPattern` or `lineNumber`; `matchPattern` + `replace` for `replace`.
`appendIfMissing` makes an append idempotent (e.g. hosts-file entries).

configKeys.description: append | prepend | insert | replaceLine | delete | replace.
1-based line for insert/replaceLine (and one delete selector).
Append only when the content is not already present.
auto (default) | utf8 | utf8-bom | utf16le | utf16be | ascii.
append/prepend only: create the file when absent.
Report what would change without writing.

generateText.description: Generate a cryptographically-secure RANDOM string — ids, tokens, GUIDs, password charsets (engine-local).
promptNotes: This is NOT an AI/LLM activity despite the name — it produces random characters, not generated prose. To have a model write text, use `llmQuery`.
`password` is only a charset preset (letters+digits+symbols); it does NOT guarantee password-policy complexity.

configKeys.description: alphanumeric (default) | alphabetic | numeric | hex | guid | password | custom.
Output length (1–1024, default 16; ignored for guid).

llmQuery.description: Call an OpenAI-compatible endpoint — prompt in, answer text out (engine-local).
promptNotes: This is THE activity for calling an AI model during a run. Use it whenever the workflow needs a model to summarize, classify, extract or draft something — never hand-build an LLM HTTP call with `restApi` or Invoke-RestMethod.
Uses the ACTIVE LLM profile (Llm:ActiveProfileId → Llm:Profiles:<id>) by default, so baseUrl/model/apiKey can normally be left empty. Requires Llm:Enabled=true and a resolvable active profile.
{{step.output}} is the answer text; token params are '' when the server omits usage.

configKeys.description: Optional system message; empty = passthrough (no default).
Override the active profile's endpoint (absolute http/https; cloud-metadata endpoints are blocked). A URL ending in /responses speaks the OpenAI Responses API, otherwise chat completions.
Override the active profile's bearer key (secret; redacted on export/MCP).
Override the active profile's max output tokens (> 0).
Sampling temperature 0..2 (per-node only; omitted = provider default).
Set response_format=json_object. The answer is NOT parsed/validated by the activity.
inline (default) | file — where the XML comes from.
single (default) | all. 'all' returns a JSON array of every match; 'single' fails when the XPath matches more than one node.
inline (default) | file — where the JSON comes from.
single (default) | all. 'all' returns a JSON array of every match; 'single' fails when the JSONPath matches more than one token.

promptNotes: Each entry of `cases` is {name, condition}, where `condition` uses the same AST as an edge `conditionExpression` and its `type` field is MANDATORY. Route downstream with edge conditions on {{step.param.case}} == "<name>".

configKeys.description: Ordered cases, each {name, condition}. First match wins.
Name reported when no case matches (default "default").
N for waitNofM. Note: the key is `requiredCount`, not `n`.

forEach.description: Iterate over a collection, running a child workflow per item (control flow).
promptNotes: forEach delegates each item to a child workflow — set `childWorkflowNameOrId`. The item and index are passed to the child as manual.* parameters named by `itemParameterName` / `indexParameterName`.

configKeys.description: How to parse `items`: auto (default) | json | lines. 'auto' tries JSON when the value starts with [ or {, else splits on newlines. There is no CSV mode — a comma-separated string parses as ONE item.
Child parameter name receiving the item.
Child parameter name receiving the 0-based index.
Additional static inputs passed to every child run.
Keep iterating after an item fails.

promptNotes: The child is addressed by ONE key, `workflowNameOrId` — there is no separate workflowId/workflowName key. Name lookup is exact-case first, then case-insensitive; ambiguous names fail the step.
With waitForCompletion=true the child's returnData is mirrored as param.*; system outputs __executionId/__status/__workflowId/__workflowName are always present. Max call depth is 10.

configKeys.description: Inputs passed as manual.* to the child.
Block for the child and mirror its returnData (default true).
How long to wait for the child.

returnData.description: Return data to the parent / mark workflow output (control flow).

configKeys.description: Key/value map; keys become downstream {{…}} param outputs and the workflow contract.

promptNotes: Parameter `type` is always the string literal "string" even for conceptually numeric values, and `default` must be a string or null — never a number or boolean.

signatureMode `header` (default) checks X-Webhook-Secret. `nodepilot-hmac-v2` requires a CSPRNG secret of at least 32 bytes plus X-NodePilot-Timestamp and a unique X-NodePilot-Delivery-Id. Legacy body-only `hmac` is rejected.

configKeys.description: Shared secret (secret value). May be mandatory via Webhook:RequireSecret.
JSONPath extractions from the body into extra manual.* params.

fileWatcherTrigger.description: FileSystemWatcher trigger — fires on file-system changes in a directory.

databaseTrigger.description: Timer + SELECT-polling trigger — fires when the query's sentinel value changes between polls.
promptNotes: The trigger query must be literal SQL — {{...}} templates are rejected, because trigger queries run before any step exists and have no variable context.

Change detection is sentinel-based, not row-based: the poll loop compares the FIRST COLUMN OF THE FIRST ROW against the previous poll and fires when it differs. Write a query that returns a changing scalar (MAX(Id), COUNT(*), MAX(UpdatedAt)); a query that keeps returning the same rows never fires.
The trigger's own outputs are {{step.param.dbSentinel}} (new value) and {{step.param.dbPrevious}} (previous value) — the matched rows themselves are not passed to downstream steps.

configKeys.description: SELECT to poll; its first column of the first row is the sentinel.
Named connection ref (preferred; may be required by Trigger:Database:RequireConnectionRef).

promptNotes: Only Application and System are readable by default; any other log must be added to Trigger:EventLog:AllowedLogs by an admin.
The trigger's outputs are {{step.param.eventId}}, {{step.param.eventSource}}, {{step.param.eventEntryType}}, {{step.param.eventMessage}} and {{step.param.eventTimeWritten}}.

configKeys.description: Regex the event message must match (500 ms per-match timeout; a timing-out entry is skipped).
Manual-run only: how far back the sample scan looks (default 5). The live listener never replays history.
